description: REQ-103 (and its FIND-003 resolution note, and verification-architecture.md's Purity Boundary Map row for lock.mjs) claims the colony-spawn mutual-exclusion critical section is 'wrapped by the existing withGigLock-equivalent helper (or a directly analogous withColonyLock("colony-spawn", fn)) using the SAME lock.mjs module, not a reimplementation' -- 'a new lock KEY on an EXISTING lock MECHANISM.' But the actual, real function this claims to reuse unmodified, `~/anicca/skills/economy/gig/lib/lock.mjs::withGigLock`, has the signature `withGigLock(statePath, lockKey, fn, opts)` (lock.mjs:187) -- `statePath` is a MANDATORY first positional argument, and `lockPaths()` (lock.mjs:78-82) derives the actual lock-file location as `path.join(path.dirname(statePath), 'locks', lockKey + '.lock')`. The lock file's real, physical identity therefore depends on BOTH `statePath`'s directory AND `lockKey` -- not on `lockKey` alone. REQ-103's EARS/Acceptance-Criteria never specifies what `statePath` value the colony-spawn caller(s) must pass. This is not a cosmetic omission: if two different code entry points that both evaluate REQ-102/103 (e.g. automaton's own cron-driven wake vs. a separately-scheduled evaluation -- REQ-106's own first edge case explicitly describes exactly this scenario as one this increment's lock design 'already handles') pass two DIFFERENT `statePath` values (e.g. one anchored at `ledger.js`'s ledger file, another at `colony-wallets.json`, another at a new dedicated state file nobody named), `lockPaths()` resolves to two DIFFERENT physical lock files under two different `locks/` directories -- both callers would then successfully acquire 'the colony-spawn lock' simultaneously, because they are not actually contending for the same file. This silently defeats REQ-103's entire stated purpose ('ensure that at most ONE of them actually proceeds') despite every other part of REQ-103 (the reused `isLockStale` predicate, the atomic `fs.rename` reclaim, the heartbeat) being correctly inherited. PROP-103a's own proof method ('two Promise.all-raced calls into withColonyLock("colony-spawn", fn)') only proves mutual exclusion WITHIN A SINGLE TEST PROCESS sharing one implicit statePath choice -- it does not, and as specified cannot, prove that every REAL call site in the eventual Phase 3 implementation is anchored to the same statePath, because the spec never names one canonical statePath for this lock to require Phase 3 code to converge on.

evidence.snippet: The colony-spawn critical section ... is wrapped by the existing `withGigLock`-equivalent helper (or a directly analogous `withColonyLock("colony-spawn", fn)`) using the SAME `lock.mjs` module, not a reimplementation.

additionalEvidence.note: actual exported signature: withGigLock(statePath, lockKey, fn, opts) -- statePath is mandatory and never optional
lockPaths() derives the real lock file path from BOTH statePath's directory and lockKey, not lockKey alone
REQ-106's own edge case describes exactly the multi-caller-on-one-host scenario that a mismatched statePath would silently break
PROP-103a's proof method never specifies or requires a single canonical statePath across call sites
